learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the crucial process of finding, hiring, training, and retaining the absolute best people for the right jobs!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Putting the right people in the right jobs at the right time. It involves manpower planning, recruitment, selection, placement, induction, training, and performance appraisal.
Searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply. It can be Internal (Transfers, Promotions) or External (Campus placement, Web publishing, Ads).
Choosing the best candidate from the pool of applicants. It is 'negative' because the number of rejected candidates is usually higher than those selected.
1. Preliminary Screening -> 2. Selection Tests (IQ, Aptitude, Personality) -> 3. Employment Interview -> 4. Reference Checks -> 5. Selection Decision -> 6. Medical Exam -> 7. Job Offer.
Training is imparting specific skills to do a specific job (e.g., learning to operate a machine). Development is overall growth of the employee (e.g., leadership seminars for future roles).

fun_activity.title: 🕵️ The Ultimate Interviewer
fun_activity.instructions: You are hiring a manager for a toy store. Write down 3 different types of selection tests (like an intelligence test or a personality test) and specify exactly what you want to measure in the candidate!

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember: Recruitment is a positive process (encouraging more people to apply), Selection is a negative process (eliminating unqualified candidates).
📌 Internal sources of recruitment are cheaper and boost morale but stop 'fresh blood' (new ideas) from entering the organization.
📌 Case studies often ask to identify the specific type of selection test (e.g., Trade test measures existing skills, Aptitude measures potential to learn).
quick_recap: ⭐ Staffing is closely linked to Human Resource Management (HRM).
⭐ Vestibule training involves training employees on dummy machines before they work on actual expensive machinery.
⭐ Placement means the employee occupying the position, and Induction is introducing them to the organization.
